title: Orchard and Vow
premise: Mirabel Eastwick built her café and her careful life on the belief that her testimony, given at fifteen against the man who burned down her family's orchard, had finally been buried. When a lost letter surfaces—postmarked eleven years ago from Callum Reeve, the boy who took the blame for a fire she actually set—it reveals he never stopped protecting her, and that he is returning to Salt Hollow as the town's new harbormaster. As her café teeters on foreclosure and old neighbors begin asking questions the letter makes dangerous to answer, Mirabel must choose between confessing the truth she let him carry and losing him again. She confesses publicly at the season's last ferry departure, trading her reputation for his freedom; Callum stays, the town slowly forgives, and they rebuild both the orchard and the café together.
about_author: Ansel Voss is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing love stories on the backs of order tickets in coastal towns much like Salt Hollow. Known for romances where forgiveness costs something real, Voss lives off-season on a peninsula with a stubborn dog and an even more stubborn sourdough starter.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Flour Tin
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. While packing up her failing café ahead of a final bank deadline, Mirabel finds an unopened letter hidden years ago in a flour tin—Callum's handwriting, postmarked eleven years back, telling her he knew the fire was hers and forgave her anyway. The emotional beat is vertigo: fifteen years of carefully rationed guilt collapse into one envelope, just as Callum himself walks past her window, home at last.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Callum, newly installed as harbormaster, seeks Mirabel out pretending the letter never existed, while she discovers he served time partly because she stayed silent—and that her silence bought the goodwill that once saved her café's lease. Rising tension: a bank notice gives her thirty days, and a nosy councilwoman begins connecting the fire, the letter, and the new harbormaster. The beat is longing laced with dread.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. On the night of the final autumn ferry—the point after which Callum has said he'll leave Salt Hollow for good—Mirabel interrupts the dockside gathering to confess publicly that she set the orchard fire and let a boy take the blame. The crowd's shock, the councilwoman's triumph, and Callum's stunned face converge as she offers the truth instead of another piece of her heart. The beat is terror becoming release.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. In the aftermath, Mirabel loses the lease but gains something stranger: neighbors who bring cuttings from surviving orchard trees, and a judge willing to revisit the old case on new testimony. Callum chooses to stay through winter, and together they reopen the café inside the restored orchard barn. The beat is earned peace—love no longer lent in pieces, but given whole.
